objective: Formalize O_calculus as the typed operator calculus governing admissible orientation transformations over RT and aRT structures.

trigger.unlocked_by: aRT promoted to typed formal object

formal_definition.title: Formal Principle 5.X: Orientation Calculus O_calculus
formal_definition.core_definition: O_calculus is the typed calculus of admissible transformations among orientation conditions over RT and aRT structures.
formal_skeleton: O := { o_k | o_k preserves typed admissible continuation over X, X in RT union aRT }
NavT : O_k x R_<-> x A_adm x T -> O_{k+1}
o_a sim_O o_b iff o_a and o_b preserve the same admissible closure class under bounded deformation
id_O(X) = X where closure_class(X), admissibility_status(X), and typed_identity(X) are preserved
O_b circ O_a is defined iff codomain(O_a) is an admissible domain for O_b
failure_conditions: FAIL_O_001: orientation degeneracy prevents selection of a determinate admissible class
FAIL_O_002: distinction collapses below operative floor epsilon
FAIL_O_003: closure support fails for the typed operand
FAIL_O_005: admissible continuation set becomes empty
FAIL_O_006: composition attempts to chain incompatible orientation classes
formal_definition.anti_reification_note: Orientation transformations do not move objects through space. They retune admissible relation-patterns over RT and aRT structures.

appendix_f_update.note: O_calculus no longer listed as incomplete missing formalism after minimum formal typing and failure rules were added.

forbidden: claim that orientation is a proven closure driver

minimum_completed: O_composition rule defined as partial or context-bound
success_condition.result: O_calculus reduced from incomplete formal debt to typed provisional operator calculus.

governance_note: This patch is a formal scaffold closure only. It does not close bridges, promote physics applications, or certify orientation as a proven closure driver.
